title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Offshore wind slams tech: Nasdaq futures down nearly 2%
conditions.summary: AI spending worries after Tesla, Meta and IBM results, plus Brent oil above $110, have futures clearly lower and the VIX up about 10%. Early quotes.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: Early quotes (about 5:30 AM ET): S&P 500 futures about -1.0%, Nasdaq 100 -1.7%, Dow -0.6%, Russell 2000 -0.8%.
Wednesday close: S&P 500 +0.6% to 7,757, Nasdaq +1.05%, Dow +0.7%.
10-year Treasury yield eased to about 5.08% in a flight to safety.
Brent crude up 3% to about $112, near a five-month high, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia; WTI near $99.
Gold about -1.1% near $4,100; bitcoin down about 3% near $82,000; VIX up about 10% to 18.4.
Asia: sharp losses on AI spending doubts, led by Hong Kong and South Korea's Kospi; the Bank of Korea held rates.
Europe: lower; the CAC 40 fell over 1% early and France's 10-year yield topped 5%, the highest since 2002.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:30 AM CT: Initial jobless claims, consensus 200K (prior 199K); continuing claims seen at 1.72M.
This morning: Kansas City Fed manufacturing survey and Conference Board leading index (prior -0.1% m/m).
Treasury auctions $26B of 5-year TIPS today.
No Fed speakers scheduled; the Fed meets next week and is expected to hold, with a December hike still priced in.
Main macro story: oil above $110 and French yields above 5% are reviving inflation and bond-market worries.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Tesla: Q3 adj. EPS $0.48 beat; capex plan cut to about $20B; shares down about 5% premarket.
Meta: revenue $64.6B beat with a stronger Q4 outlook, but a $9.9B legal charge hit EPS; early trading mixed.
IBM: beat on EPS and revenue but consulting missed; shares down about 5-6%.
Texas Instruments little changed; Lam Research beat and guided Q2 EPS to $2.18-$2.48; Las Vegas Sands missed.
Qiagen agreed to an all-cash EQT takeover at EUR 46.50 a share, a 40% premium; SAP up 2% on cloud growth.
Before the open today: Procter & Gamble, Lockheed Martin, Honeywell, Union Pacific, Blackstone, Comcast, American Airlines.
After the close today: Western Digital, Newmont, Bloom Energy, Deckers, Boston Beer.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: IBM (International Business Machines): -5.7% — beat but consulting revenue missed.
TSLA (Tesla): -5.3% — capex cut and cautious Optimus and robotaxi outlook.
INTC (Intel): -5.1% — chip selloff on AI spending worries.
SMCI (Super Micro Computer): -4.7% — AI hardware names under pressure.
AMD, QCOM, MRVL, AVGO, MU: -2.9% to -5.3% — broad semiconductor selloff.
NVDA (Nvidia): -2.4% — AI trade lower.
SPCX (SpaceX): -2.3% — giving back gains after Wednesday's post-earnings jump.
KMI (Kinder Morgan): +1.5% — Q3 profit beat and record $14.4B backlog.

sections.title: Business News
items: Bloomberg reports SpaceX and Tesla are pursuing a merger by H1 2027; neither has commented and no filings back it.
Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs and launching a GBP 500M buyback.
Chinese regulators summoned major e-commerce platforms over product quality, sending Alibaba to a two-month low.
Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia pushed Brent crude toward a five-month high.
France's 10-year yield breached 5% amid budget paralysis and nationwide unrest.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT jobless claims (consensus 200K).
Brent above $110 and the 10-year near 5.1%: both key pressure gauges for stocks.
Western Digital after the close for a read on AI storage demand.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Thursday, October twenty-second, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Gus the wonder dog is curled up on his beach towel by the cabana door, one ear up. Give the Dawn Patrol a big hello, Gus! Conditions are poor this morning, with a stiff offshore wind knocking tech back after yesterday's rally. These are early quotes. S and P 500 futures were down about one percent. Nasdaq 100 futures were down about one point seven percent. Dow futures were down about half a percent. The VIX jumped about ten percent to just above eighteen. That's gnarly. The ten-year yield eased to about five point oh eight percent. Brent crude climbed more than three percent to about one hundred twelve dollars after new Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia. Gold slipped about one percent, and bitcoin fell about three percent. Overnight, Asia wiped out, with steep losses in Hong Kong and South Korea on doubts about AI spending. Europe was lower too. Wind and weather. Weekly jobless claims land at seven thirty A M Central. The forecast is about two hundred thousand. No Fed speakers are on the calendar, and the Fed meets next week. Now the tide chart. Tesla beat on profit but cut its spending plan, and the stock slid about five percent. I B M beat too, yet fell about five percent on softer consulting sales. Over in Europe, Qiagen agreed to be bought by the private equity firm E Q T at about a forty percent premium. Now that is a clean wave. Treat time, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Procter and Gamble and Lockheed Martin report before the bell. After the close, watch Western Digital and Newmont. The lineup. It's a rough paddle for chip stocks. Intel, A M D, Micron and Broadcom were down roughly three to five percent, and Super Micro fell nearly five percent. Kinder Morgan bucked the trend, up about one and a half percent. Beach talk. Bloomberg reports SpaceX and Tesla are aiming for a merger in the first half of twenty twenty-seven. Neither company has confirmed it. Barclays is cutting five thousand jobs and buying back five hundred million pounds of stock. Sets to watch. Seven thirty A M Central for jobless claims. Oil above one hundred ten dollars. And Western Digital after the close, for a read on AI storage demand. Want a read on a different break?
